According to incomplete statistics, in‌ the first half of 2021 alone, the topic “snow-capped ⁤mountains were gled again in Chengdu ” went viral and flooded the screen of Chengdu people ‍26 times. according to statistics, the snow-capped ⁢mountains were caught sight of in Chengdu for a total of 35 times in 2016, and the figure rose to 75 in 2020.
Source: THE STORY OF CHENGDU, a Time-Honored City of ⁢Heart-Soothing Character
It is ​indeed the biggest building in the world; 16 Wembley⁤ stadiums could fit underneath its ‍vast roof. But the New ‌Century Global Center, a behemoth in the central city of Chengdu which …
Source: Shadowy Chinese billionaire behind world’s largest building vanishes
The “Snow Village” in Chengdu is located in Jingshan Village, Datong town, Qionglai, Chengdu, Sichuan. It ⁢is a small attraction within the Nanshan Resort Area.During the recent Chinese New ‍Year holiday, the “Snow​ Village” attracted a large number of‌ tourists with its “beautiful snowy scenes” ‌of forests and small cottages depicted in ‌promotional photos. ‌The village​ decided to produce as if it⁣ were real snow using cotton and soapy water. After placing cotton throughout the village, it was decorated like snow, and it was opened on ​the 29th of last month.
Tourists who visited the village in anticipation of snow piled up were absurd to see cotton, not eyes. They expressed their complaints such as “I’m fully‌ deceived” and “I have not paid this money to see the⁢ cotton.”
As criticism continued, the Namba Osan Tourism Authority posted an apology on WeChat on the 8th and decided to temporarily suspend the village sales from the‌ next day. the Namba Osan Tourism⁢ District said, “The snow village project was ‍created based⁤ on the weather forecast ‍that the temperature would‌ fall‌ and snow ⁣was falling during the spring.”
“During the Chunje holiday, all the cotton was removed, and the area ⁤was able to⁣ return to the original.”
The domestic netizens who have heard the news are also absurd. Some netizens responded by saying, “Is it⁣ a fake eye now?”
Source: Fake Snow Scene Made of Cotton: Chengdu’s “Snow Village” Tourist Area
Interview:‌ Teh Enchanting and Controversial Snow ⁤Scenes of Chengdu have ⁣you ‍ever wondered⁢ about the snowy phenomena that have captivated ‌the hearts of Chengdu residents? From⁤ the captivating rise in snow-capped mountain sightings to the recent ‍controversy⁢ over fake snow in a popular tourist attraction, the story behind ‌these snowy scenes is as ‌complex as it is‍ intriguing. In ⁣this exclusive⁢ interview, our Senior Editor, Jane Doe, delves into these issues with⁤ renowned specialist dr. Li Wei,⁤ an expert on ⁣regional ‍tourism and environmental impacts.
The Phenomenon of Snow-Capped Mountains in Chengdu jane ⁤Doe: ‍Dr. Li,​ the statistics indicate that snow-capped mountains in Chengdu have become a more ⁢frequent ​sight over the years. Can you shed some light‌ on the factors contributing to this trend?
Dr.⁤ Li Wei: ​ Certainly.Chengdu’s location and climatic changes have played ​a significant role. ​Over the past decade, weather ⁢patterns​ have become more ‍unpredictable, leading to⁣ sporadic but notable snowfall‌ events. additionally, increased awareness and media ⁢coverage have made these rare events more visible‍ to⁣ the public.This has led ‌to the “snow-capped mountains in Chengdu” topic going viral ⁣on social media multiple times.
The⁤ New Century Global Center Jane Doe: shifting focus slightly, the ⁢New ​Century ‌Global Center in Chengdu is​ reported to‍ be the largest⁢ building in ⁣the world. Though, there have been controversies surrounding it’s developers, particularly a shadowy billionaire who has​ reportedly vanished amid a corruption scandal. how does this affect the ‌perception of ⁤such large-scale developments?
Dr.Li Wei: The controversies around the developers cast a shadow over the or ‍else extraordinary architectural feat of ​the New Century Global Center. Public trust in large-scale projects ⁢has been compromised.The abrupt disappearance of the key figure involved has‌ led to⁢ increased scrutiny of the⁤ ethical standards applied in large infrastructure developments in China. This has wider‍ implications for future projects, requiring greater openness and ethical conduct.
The “Snow⁤ Village” Controversy Jane Doe: the “Snow Village” in Chengdu​ recently made⁤ headlines for using cotton instead of ​real snow, leading ‍to widespread criticism.Can you provide some insights into this incident and its impact ⁤on the region’s ⁤tourism?
Dr. Li Wei: The “Snow Village” incident underscores the⁤ gulf between expectations and reality in tourism marketing. Tourists‌ were misled by promotional materials,‍ leading ⁢to ⁣severe disappointment. such⁤ incidents damage the​ credibility of ​local attractions and can deter future visitors. The temporary​ suspension of the village’s operations⁣ shows ‌the ​seriousness of the issue ⁢and signals the need ⁢for better alignment between marketing and reality, and more importantly, environmental sustainability.
Future Outlook Jane Doe: Given these developments,​ where ​do you see the future of snow-related tourism and large-scale developments in Chengdu heading?
Dr. Li Wei: Moving forward,there will be a greater emphasis‍ on‌ ethical practice⁢ and transparency. Developers and promoters⁤ must adhere ⁢to the principles of accuracy and sustainability. furthermore, as‌ climatic ⁤uncertainties continue, there will be increased focus on ‍environmental resilience and authenticity. This will help ⁤rebuild public trust and ensure‌ long-term sustainability ‍for attractions and ⁢developments alike.
conclusion The snow-capped mountains, the colossal New Century Global Center, ‌and the “Snow village” incident offer a multifaceted look at the evolving⁤ landscape of Chengdu.⁣ While⁢ these elements highlight both the marvels and complexities of modern development, they also point to the ⁣critical need for ethical practices and transparency. Dr. Li Wei’s‌ insights have illuminated ‌the path forward, emphasizing‌ the⁣ importance of honesty and environmental ⁤consciousness in shaping the ‌future⁣ of Chengdu’s tourism sector.
